questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: The suffix -oso and two of its neighbours

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «The suffix -oso indicates presence or abundance of the quality named, so famoso means full of fame.» La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: Aplicando «The suffix -oso and two of its neighbours» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?

answer.exemplar: The suffix -oso indicates presence or abundance of the quality named, so famoso means full of fame.

questions.explanation: -oso means full of the quality. The suffix -oso indicates presence or abundance of the quality named, so famoso means full of fame. The tempting reading, "Famoso means full of fame", stops short of applying the operation fully, so it is not the value the case yields. Here the stem reads 'Aplicando «The suffix -oso and two of its neighbours» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?'; the model answer opens with 'The suffix -oso indicates presence or abundance of the quality named, so famoso means full of fame.'.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Prefixes that fix the meaning of a whole word

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «des-, reversing or removing the action.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: La nota se contrasta con «Identify the prefix des- / des- means undo. / Prefixes that fix the meaning of a whole word». ¿qué respuesta queda respaldada?

options.text: des-, reversing or removing the action

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: the prefix des- reverses or removes the action. On that basis "des-, reversing or removing the action" is the supported choice. Option A ("pre-, placing before") fails because it confuses des- with pre-; Option D ("in-, negating the base word") fails because it confuses des- with in-; Option C ("re-, repeating the action") fails because it confuses des- with re-.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: The five noun suffixes that build most abstract vocabulary

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «-mento, as in momento.» La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: El indicio de este ítem es «Name abstract suffixes / -mento comes from results. / The five noun suffixes that build most abstract vocabulary». ¿qué opción lo cumple?

options.misconception: confuses a verbal suffix with a result one
confuses a state suffix with a result one
confuses a state suffix with a result one

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: -mento builds abstract nouns from results, as in momento. On that basis "-mento, as in momento" is the supported choice. Option A ("-ción, as in canción") fails because it confuses a verbal suffix with a result one; Option B ("-dad, as in ciudad") fails because it confuses a state suffix with a result one; Option D ("-tad, as in libertad") fails because it confuses a state suffix with a result one.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: The feminine of a profession in -ado across varieties

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «soldado, unchanged.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: La nota se contrasta con «The feminine of a profession in -ado across varieties». ¿qué respuesta queda respaldada?

options.misconception: reverses the direction of the reasoning the passage sets out

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: soldado keeps the same form for women in many varieties. On that basis "soldado, unchanged" is the supported choice. Option A ("soldada, adding a") fails because it reverses the direction of the reasoning that settles the feminine of a profession in -ado across varieties; Option B ("soldadina, adding an extra suffix") fails because it invents a non-standard feminine form; Option C ("soldad, dropping the final o") fails because it shortens the word incorrectly.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Nouns in -ista and the gender of the person named

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «Nouns in -ista are common gender, so artista stays the same for both men and women, and only the article changes.» « la artista » La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: La nota se contrasta con «Identify -ista as common gender / Only the article changes. / Nouns in -ista and the gender of the person named». ¿qué respuesta queda respaldada?

answer.exemplar: Nouns in -ista are common gender, so artista stays the same for both men and women, and only the article changes.

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: -ista nouns do not change form by gender. On that basis "Nouns in -ista are common gender, so artista stays the same for both men and women, and only…" is the supported choice.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Forming an adverb in -mente from an adjective

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «rápidamente, adding -mente to the feminine form.» « rápido » Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Con la pista «Form an adverb with -mente / Use the feminine form plus -mente. / Forming an adverb in -mente from an adjective / rápid, dropping the adjective ending», ¿qué opción se ajusta realmente al fragmento?

options.text: rápidamente, adding -mente to the feminine form
rápidomente, adding -mente to the masculine form
options.misconception: uses the masculine form instead of feminine

options.text: rápido mente, writing two separate words

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: adverbs in -mente use the feminine form of the adjective: rápidamente. On that basis "rápidamente, adding -mente to the feminine form" is the supported choice. Option D ("rápid, dropping the adjective ending") fails because it shortens the adjective incorrectly; Option B ("rápidomente, adding -mente to the masculine form") fails because it uses the masculine form instead of feminine; Option C ("rápido mente, writing two separate words") fails because it fails to join the suffix.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Replacing muy before an adverb or a longer adjective

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «rapidísimamente, using the superlative.» « muy rápidamente » Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Con la pista «Use the superlative form.», ¿qué opción se ajusta realmente al fragmento?

options.misconception: uses a comparative instead of superlative

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: before an adverb, muy can be replaced by a superlative form. On that basis "rapidísimamente, using the superlative" is the supported choice. Option A ("más rápidamente, using más") fails because it uses a comparative instead of superlative; Option C ("muy rápidamente, keeping muy") fails because it keeps the weaker intensifier; Option D ("rápido muy, reversing the order") fails because it reverses word order.
